title: AWS Network Firewall & Traffic Inspection
summary: Stateful VPC firewalls, centralized inspection VPCs and DNS-layer filtering.
tldr: **AWS Network Firewall** is a managed, stateful VPC firewall with IDS/IPS (**Suricata-compatible** rules) and domain allow/deny lists. Traffic reaches it by **routing** to its endpoints.
Many VPCs? Build one **inspection VPC** on Transit Gateway with the firewall (and NAT gateways) and route spoke egress through it.
Must use a **third-party appliance** vendor? Put the appliances behind a **Gateway Load Balancer** and route to GWLB endpoints.
Blocking malicious domains or DNS tunneling at resolution time is **Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall**.

keyFacts.text: An **edge route table** on the internet gateway sends inbound traffic to the firewall endpoint before it reaches the ALB subnets.
Stateful rule groups can allow only listed FQDNs (from TLS SNI or HTTP Host) for egress filtering.
Gateway Load Balancer uses GENEVE encapsulation on port 6081 to pass traffic transparently to appliances, and scales them as a target group.
Deploy firewall endpoints in each AZ and keep routing AZ-symmetric so stateful inspection sees both directions.

traps: Security groups and NACLs can't filter by domain name or do deep packet inspection.
WAF only sees HTTP(S) to supported resources; it can't inspect general egress traffic.
Deploying a firewall in every spoke VPC works but is not the central, lowest-overhead answer when there are dozens of VPCs.
Asymmetric routing across AZs breaks stateful inspection.
